_note: Stage 4 evidence sets. These are NOT belief fixtures — no belief, edge, confidence or valence is authored here. Each entry is a list of observations handed to BeliefExtractor; the web is whatever the model builds. That is the whole point of the stage: structure must arrive from the extractor, not from us.

flat.revision: v3, 2026-08-09. Revised after the Stage 4 pilot, which is what a pilot is for; the structured scenarios and their predictions are untouched.
flat.note: Third design. v1 used facts about the user, and the extractor prompt licenses generalising from a known user to humans as a class. v2 replaced them with facts I believed were from disjoint domains - but two of the four (British-English docs, a pinned Debian image) are both REPOSITORY CONVENTIONS, and on the API path the model correctly hubbed them under 'this repository fixes its environment and style choices explicitly'. That was a real entailment my fixture handed it, not a false positive; the CLI had merely been too sparse to find it. v3 uses four subjects with no shared domain at all - local timing, geography, music history, an industrial standard - so any hub over them would have to be vacuous.
